cells.reason: The anchor is the California SWRCB hexavalent-chromium MCL of 0.010 mg/L for water delivered by public water systems (scope 'drinking water'; the regulation page states it 'is a drinking-water standard, not a food limit' and 'should not be compared directly to a food-occurrence concentration'); a drinking-water row is not a food-content row, so basis condition (b) fails for an as-sold dried-seaweed content cell. The register holds no food-content Cr-VI maximum level in any jurisdiction (the only Cr-VI rows are drinking water, toy migration, textiles, leather, RoHS, tattoo ink and fertiliser), and GB 2762-2025 Table 7 expressly sets total chromium only. The cell should be published as a species-bounded cell, Cr-VI <= total Cr, with the parent total as its number: 1000 on this packet's adjudication of the Cr parent (2000 if the milk-powder parent is retained), never a read-across from a water MCL.
